source: Energy starts with the Sun. Producers (plants) make food; consumers eat plants or other animals; decomposers break down dead things. A food web is many food chains joined together.
Reading the arrows backward. In a food chain the arrow points from the food to the eater: grass → rabbit means the rabbit eats the grass.
A rabbit eats grass. A fox eats the rabbit. The energy in the fox's dinner came, in the end, from the Sun.

Producers (plants and algae) make food from sunlight. Consumers eat other living things: herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both. Decomposers (mushrooms, bacteria, worms help too) break down dead plants and animals and return their minerals to the soil.
A food chain. Each arrow points from the food to the eater.
Most animals eat more than one thing, and are eaten by more than one thing. When we draw all the chains together, they make a food web.
If the rabbits all disappeared, the foxes and hawks would have less to eat, and the grass might grow taller. A change in one part of a web changes the others.
In the chain seeds → mouse → owl, what does the owl eat?
The arrow points from the food to the eater.
The arrow into the owl comes from the mouse.
Reading the arrows backward. "Grass → rabbit" means energy goes from the grass to the rabbit: the rabbit eats the grass.
